Let each individual customer account authorize the app via OAuth

prohibitions: Uploading, editing, moving, or deleting files or folders
guide.summary: Each customer account authorizes the app through Dropbox OAuth 2.0 and receives a user-scoped token. The app is limited to App Folder data, and files.metadata.read covers listing and continuation.
guide.recommendation: Each customer account authorizes the app through Dropbox OAuth 2.0 and receives a user-scoped token. The app is limited to App Folder data, and files.metadata.read covers listing and continuation.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth 2.0 authorization for each customer account
findings.detail: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0 to authorize access to a user's data. The user is redirected to Dropbox to authorize the app, is sent back with an authorization code, and the app exchanges that code for an access token used in Bearer headers.
findings.appliesWhen: Each individual customer account connects to the app.

evidence.quote: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0
In this flow: The user will be redirected to Dropbox to authorize your app to access their Dropbox data.
Your application exchanges the authorization code for an access token that can be used to make secure calls to the Dropbox API (not shown)

findings.title: Register the app and configure redirect URIs before testing
findings.detail: The app must be registered in the Developer Console to obtain an app key and secret (client_id and client_secret). Exact redirect URIs must be registered under the OAuth 2 section of the Settings tab.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you’ll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the Developer Console
. That page will guide you through the process of registering your app, selecting permissions, and obtaining an app key and secret (a.k.a. client_id and client_secret ) and inputting redirect
You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console

findings.title: Select App Folder content access at app creation
findings.detail: App Folder access lets the app take actions allowed by its scopes only within its app folder under /apps. Full Dropbox access would expose all data in the account, which this request does not require.
findings.appliesWhen: When creating the app, so the listing is limited to the app folder.

findings.title: files.metadata.read grant for listing names and metadata
findings.detail: files.metadata.read is the required scope for list_folder and list_folder/continue. It covers metadata listing only and does not grant file content download or write operations.
findings.appliesWhen: Selected in the app Permissions tab and requested during authorization. The boundary is limited to the App Folder when App Folder access is chosen.

evidence.quote: Required scope: files.metadata.read Endpoint format: RPC
The selected scopes are applied to your access token and determine which API calls your application is allowed to execute. This level of access is then communicated to the end
, you’ll choose from different scopes in the ‘Permissions’ tab.

steps.title: Register the Dropbox app with App Folder access and files.metadata.read
steps.detail: In the Dropbox Developer Console, create a Scoped access app with App folder access, enable files.metadata.read on the Permissions tab, save changes, and register the exact redirect URI under the OAuth 2 section of Settings. Copy the app key (client_id) and app secret (client_secret) into the developer's secure configuration. The authorization-code flow with a server-side client_secret is used for this first test.
steps.doneWhen: The app exists with App folder access, files.metadata.read is enabled and saved, a redirect URI is registered, and client_id and client_secret are available to the developer. Expected output: a Developer Console app page showing these settings.

client_secret: app secret, stored server-side only

steps.title: Send a test user through the Dropbox OAuth consent flow and verify the callback
steps.detail: Open the Dropbox authorization URL in a browser while signed in as a test customer account, approve access, and confirm Dropbox redirects to the registered redirect URI with a code query parameter and the state value if one was sent. Do not exchange the code yet.
steps.doneWhen: The browser lands on the registered redirect URI containing code=... and, if sent, the matching state value. Expected output: the redirect URL with the code parameter; no token is requested in this step.

evidence.quote: Construct a Dropbox authorization URL , with your application’s client_id and redirect_uri (if applicable) and specifying the response_type of code , and present it to the user

fields: CLIENT_ID: app key from registration step
REDIRECT_URI: exact URI registered in Settings
STATE: random value generated by the developer, checked on callback

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for a user access token and refresh token
steps.detail: Exchange the code returned to the redirect URI for an access token using the documented token endpoint with the client_secret on the server. Request token_access_type=offline at authorization so a refresh token is returned for later continuation. Store the access token and refresh token securely. Expected output: JSON with access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in and refresh_token.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns access_token and refresh_token with expires_in. Expected output: JSON containing these fields; the access token is never printed in logs.

evidence.quote: Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls

When using refresh tokens, your call to the /oauth2/token endpoint with the grant_type of authorization_code will return a short-lived access token and a refresh token, which should be securely stored.
Note : you’ll need to include token_access_type=offline as a parameter on your Authorization URL in order to return a refresh_token inside your access token payload.

fields: AUTH_CODE: code query parameter from the redirect in the previous step
CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET: from app registration, server-side only
REDIRECT_URI: must match the authorization request exactly

steps.title: List the first page of App Folder entries with metadata only
steps.detail: Call list_folder on the app folder root using the user's access token, with path set to the empty string for the App Folder root and recursive false. Keep the default include options. Do not call any download, upload, move, or delete endpoint. Read the returned names from entries[].name. Save the cursor and has_more values.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains entries, cursor and has_more. Expected output: JSON with entries[].name, .tag and a cursor; has_more indicates whether continuation is needed. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Required scope: files.metadata.read Endpoint format: RPC
curl -X POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/files/list_folder \

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: user token from the exchange step, server-side only
path empty string: App Folder root for App Folder access
limit: optional page size, 1-2000

steps.title: Continue listing App Folder entries until has_more is false
steps.detail: While has_more is true, call list_folder/continue with the cursor from the previous response, repeating with each new cursor. Collect entries[].name from every page. Stop when has_more is false; a single page is not a complete listing.
steps.doneWhen: A response returns has_more false. Expected output: all entries across pages collected, with the final page's has_more false.

steps.title: Verify the token cannot act outside the metadata read scope
steps.detail: Using the same user token obtained via the code flow for a single user, make one nonmutating list_folder call to a real existing path outside the App Folder supplied by the user, and inspect the response. Do not assume a specific error code; record whatever the API returns, and inspect the Permissions tab to confirm only files.metadata.read is granted. Do not call any write endpoint. The path value must be provided by the user and is not invented here.
steps.doneWhen: The response is recorded (either an error or App Folder-only data) and the Permissions tab shows only files.metadata.read. Expected output: a documented error response or App Folder-only entries.
